facts.fact: Libya's National Council for Public Freedoms and Human Rights says its draft personal data protection law, referred to the House of Representatives as an initial proposal, includes a chapter on artificial intelligence covering personal data in training and running AI systems, privacy, transparency, accountability and limiting discrimination.
facts.system: Draft national personal data protection law (AI chapter)

LBY.note: Document states nothing on government use of AI systems.
Document states nothing on AI in a sector's public system.
Document states nothing on AI models, datasets or computing built in Libya.
Document states nothing on a rule that data be kept in the country.

facts.fact: Libya's National Council for Public Freedoms and Human Rights and a House of Representatives committee began a joint review on 26 October 2026 of a draft personal data protection law, prepared by the council's national committee over more than two and a half years with a Council of Europe-appointed expert's review and referred to the House as an initial proposal.
facts.system: Draft national personal data protection law

LBY.note: Document states nothing on conditions for sending data abroad.
Document states nothing on standards body membership or adopted IT standards.
